stories.title: Brian Thomas Jr. trying to ignore trade talk, 'keep working hard' for Jaguars
stories.summary: Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. said Wednesday he isn't concerned about being the subject of recent trade rumors.
stories.detail: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr . said Wednesday he isn't concerned about being the subject of recent trade rumors. And he isn't wasting time worrying about his future with the team, either. After all, he's been there before. "Everybody's entitled to their own opinion," Thomas, a Pro Bowler as a rookie, said. "I just go out there, do what I do, and just try to go out there and be the best player I can be." For some, that opinion is that Thomas needs a change of scenery and that the Jaguars would be better off trading the third-year receiver, especially after his disappointing performance against the Houston Texans in London on Oct. 18. Thomas dropped one pass and failed to come up with a catchable throw in the first half of that game, then didn't play a snap in the second half of the 34-31 loss, later leaving the Wembley Stadium locker room without talking to reporters. On the season, Thomas now has four drops, per ESPN Research. Thomas on Wednesday said he wanted to "flush" that game and move forward with a different mindset. "Everybody goes through adversity," he said. "You've just got to keep fighting through it. That's the only way I know how to get thro…

stories.title: Jets WR Garrett Wilson says he doesn't want to be traded but does want to win
stories.summary: Jets receiver Garrett Wilson says he doesn't want to be traded but he expressed that he's frustrated by his target share and, most of all, losing.
stories.detail: FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson made two things abundantly clear Wednesday: He doesn't want to be traded, but he's extremely frustrated by his lack of involvement in the offense and, most of all, the losing. "Yeah, I want to be here, man," Wilson said. "I want to win games and that's the one thing we've been missing on here. I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I'm hopeful. "I've never been the best optimistic guy, but I've found a way and dug deep, and I've been optimistic for three, four, five years now. And that's why these [losses] each weekend hurt a little more." Wilson was visibly upset on the sideline in the fourth quarter of the Jets' 28-25 loss to the previously winless Miami Dolphins on Sunday. He was targeted only three times in the game (two catches for 26 yards), one week after he was a non-factor in a loss to the New England Patriots . His frustration, coupled with the Nov. 10 trade deadline, has fueled speculation about his desire to remain in New York. stories.title: Carlton Davis ready to make return vs. Dolphins
stories.summary: The Patriots starting cornerback has missed the last three games.
stories.detail: New England Patriots cornerback Carlton Davis III is ready to make his return to the field this Sunday against the Miami Dolphins. Davis initially injured his neck in the season opener against Seattle and missed the Week 2 contest against the Steelers. He came back for the following two weeks before missing the Patriots’ last three games. The cornerback feels his initial return was too soon, but he is now ready to go. “Just day in, day out, trying to look for ways to get better,” Davis said. “Not trying to rush the process, but really trying to be efficient, recovering, and getting back out there, being a guy that my team can depend on. “I think the worst is just sitting on the sideline, watching plays being made or being a bystander. Last year, I played in every game. This year I was looking to do the same, and it’s a bit disappointing to not be able to do that. But I’m back here and ready to go.” The Patriots secondary has not been at full force since Week 1 in Seattle. In addition to Davis, New England has played without safety Craig Woodson for one game and cornerback Christian Gonzalez for two. stories.title: Ernie Johnson says this is his final season as 'Inside the NBA' host
stories.summary: Ernie Johnson will retire as host of "Inside the NBA" after the season, saying that it was his decision to step away and that "it's just time."
stories.detail: Sports Broadcasting Hall of Famer Ernie Johnson will retire as host of "Inside the NBA" after the season, saying in a social media video Wednesday that it was his decision to step away and that "it's just time." Johnson, 70, said he would continue to work, including coverage of the NCAA men's basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports. "Just to be clear, I'm not retiring," Johnson said. "Just cutting back. ... So this is by no means the end. It's just a turning of the page. And I'll forever cherish every chapter we have written with 'Inside the NBA.'" Johnson acknowledged that he has dealt with heart issues in recent years. He said that he was doing well but that the health matters helped him realize the importance of time with family, adding "I just want to slow down a bit." "Ernie Johnson is one of sports media's most respected and beloved figures," ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro said in a statement. "For more than three decades, he has been the heart of 'Inside the NBA,' helping create one of the most iconic and entertaining studio shows in sports. We are grateful for Ernie's extraordinary contributions and look forward to celebrating him throughout the season." Johnson has wo…

stories.title: Timberwolves say Anthony Edwards will be 'good as new' after knee surgery
stories.summary: The Timberwolves believe Anthony Edwards will be "good as new" following arthroscopic surgery for a lingering injury to his right knee.
stories.detail: MINNEAPOLIS --The Minnesota Timberwolves believe Anthony Edwards will be "good as new" following arthroscopic surgery for a lingering injury to his right knee , president of basketball operations Tim Connelly said Wednesday. Edwards was scheduled for the cleanup procedure Thursday, after which the Timberwolves will have a clearer timetable for his return later this season, whether that becomes a matter of weeks or months. Connelly didn't specify the diagnosis, but Edwards was bothered by right knee pain last spring and limited to a career-low 61 games last season. He then suffered a hyperextension of his left knee in the first round of the playoffs that caused a deep bone bruise and kept him out for two games. Edwards was seen grabbing his knee with a grimace at one point Sunday during the home opener. Even after being listed as questionable to play Monday, Edwards scored 47 points in an overtime loss at Cleveland . His 133 points through four games is a franchise record. An MRI Tuesday revealed new damage for Edwards that was not detected in previous scans, which were done before training camp and during the playoffs. stories.title: Lakers rule out Luka Doncic, Ziaire Williams vs. Clippers
stories.summary: Lakers star Luka Doncic (back) and starter Ziaire Williams (foot) will not play in Wednesday's game vs. the Clippers, who will be without Rui Hachimura (quad).
stories.detail: Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic will not play against the LA Clippers on Wednesday at Intuit Dome because of back tightness, the team announced. Doncic scored 41 points in the Lakers' 136-129 home loss to the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday -- the team's first loss of the season after a 3-0 start. He leads the league with 36.0 points per game one week into the NBA season. The Lakers, playing on the second night of a back-to-back, will also be down starter Ziaire Williams due to left foot soreness. On the other side, the Clippers will be without forward Rui Hachimura , who has left quad soreness. Kobe Sanders will make his first start of the season in Hachimura's place. Hachimura scored 16 points against his former team last week in the Lakers' 125-117 win over the Clippers at Crypto.com Arena.

stories.detail: Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić has been ruled out for Wednesday’s game against the L.A. Clippers. Dončić led the Lakers in scoring in a 136-129 home loss to the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday, Oct. 27. The point guard nearly produced a double-double with 41 points, nine assists and five rebounds in 39 minutes played against Portland. It followed his 52-point game against the Utah Jazz on Sunday, Oct. 25. Dončić scored 39 points through the first three quarters of play before tying Kareem Abdul-Jabbar with 10 career 50-point games, which is the 11th most in NBA history. The Lakers guard passed Kevin Durant and Giannis Antetokounmpo, who each have nine. Dončić added his name to the franchise record books, becoming the fastest player to score 3,000 points in a Lakers uniform. The six-time All-NBA selection accomplished the feat in 95 games, beating out George Mikan (106) and Abdul-Jabbar (109). Luka Dončić injury update Dončić has been ruled out with back tightness. He was not listed on Monday's injury report ahead of the game against Portland. Coach JJ Redick is expected to talk to the media before tonight's game against the Clippers and will provide an update.
